gloss: Japanese long onion; green onion; leek

definitions.gloss: Japanese long onion; green onion; Welsh onion
definitions.explanation: A long white-and-green onion commonly used in Japanese cooking, known in English as Japanese leek, Welsh onion, or green onion. The white part is especially prized in eastern Japan.

examples.japanese: {長|なが}ねぎを{細|こま}かく{刻|きざ}んだ。
examples.english: I chopped the green onion finely.

examples.japanese: {鍋|なべ}に{長|なが}ねぎを{入|い}れると{甘|あま}みが{出|で}る。
examples.english: Adding long onion to a hot pot brings out sweetness.

examples.japanese: {味噌汁|みそしる}の{仕上|しあ}げに{長|なが}ねぎの{小口切|こぐちぎ}りを{散|ち}らすと、{風味|ふうみ}がぐっと{良|よ}くなる。
examples.english: Sprinkling thinly sliced green onion rings on miso soup as a finishing touch greatly enhances the flavor.

notes:
A compound of {長|なが}い (long) and ねぎ (onion/scallion). Refers specifically to the thick, long variety of ねぎ with a substantial white portion, as opposed to smaller varieties.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {長|なが}ねぎを{刻|きざ}む (to chop green onion)
- {長|なが}ねぎの{白|しろ}い{部分|ぶぶん} (the white part of the onion)
- {長|なが}ねぎの{小口切|こぐちぎ}り (onion sliced into thin rings)
- {長|なが}ねぎの{青|あお}い{部分|ぶぶん} (the green part of the onion)

In eastern Japan ({関東|かんとう}), the thick white part is preferred, while in western Japan ({関西|かんさい}), thinner green onions ({青|あお}ねぎ) are more commonly used. Recipes often specify {長|なが}ねぎ to distinguish from other ねぎ varieties.
